limitations: Reviewer is a separate reviewer agent session (model Sonnet 5.5, claude-sonnet-5-5) on the same host and the same account, launched by the producer session; it is not a second machine and not a human.

This is a delta review of a blanking-only change: the three packets differ from the approved v12 packets only in vendor instruction text replaced by filler. The semantic review of the scores is the previous approved review (v12, reviewer opus-independent-reviewer-deepseek-harness-cli); this review re-ran the replays and tamper controls, found all 31 metric rows of each run equal to v12 (id, state, correct, observed_eligible, decoded_eligible; the full rows with evidence also equal), and did not repeat the event-population and duplicate-rule judgments.

Vendor instruction text was blanked at equal encoded JSON string length in each native session: 185 strings per run (184 tool and schema description strings of the two request/header records, and the system string of session/title-llm-request); the filler starts with the marker '[vendor instruction text removed at equal byte length]' (cut at the string length when the original is shorter than the marker). Tool names, keys, shapes and record sizes are unchanged. Kept on purpose and judged acceptable: the title request message of about 850 characters, which is the workload prompt inside one wrapper sentence of the harness. System, runtime-context and skill-catalog text was already replaced by same-length markers in v12.

The duplicate rule (containers, membership, restatement) and the digest rule were written on 2026-10-05, after the captures of 2026-09-29/30 and after the earlier approval of this row (v8). The packets were rebuilt for these rules; observer, stdout, cache and workload bytes are byte-identical to v8; the native session bytes differ from v8 by the vendor-text blanking of this version.
Capture provenance is archived and was not re-acquired: no harness was run and no native root was reacquired; the OS statement is a post-capture attestation by operator id codex-root-operator.

The three public packets are sanitized derivatives (canonical plain JSONL) of private Zstandard parents: home paths and name are replaced by same-length aliases, and system, runtime-context, skill-catalog and tool-description text is replaced by same-length markers. Sizes and JSON shapes equal the private parents; every leaf difference is an alias, a same-length marker or a digest.

The replay depends on the host libzstd pinned by hash (1.5.7, sha256 69d8dee81bccdee425d167300d11431f3c5ecc34a3011400e536aa89f7756189); it is not bundled. Only macOS sandbox-exec isolation on this host was exercised.

Owner decision, not approved by this review: repetition 1 is the run dsh-cal-20260929-2, which was named as a calibration attempt, and the run set was not designated in the attempt ledger before scoring. It is kept by owner decision of 2026-10-04 with the disclosure in the bundled adapter document.

Binding lost to close the privacy routes: the published parent manifest keeps only three captured-file digests (bench_check.py, helper-ledger.jsonl, workload.json). The digest of the private compressed session file and all home-inventory digests except the empty lock file are zeroed. The public packet does not prove that the session file, the stdout streams, the observer base, the capture receipts and the projection cache are the captured ones. That link rests on the private parents, which a public reader cannot check.

Reviewer judgment on the read and the event population. The read is session.v4.jsonl plus the projection cache (the decoder takes attribution.reconciliation from the cache). Events: 2 prompts, assistant/message records with a text or reasoning block, tool calls by turn, step and call id, tool results. The reviewer's own content recount gives 29/64, 25/57, 25/57, equal to the packets. Restatement is tested by equality of a text argument with a string value of the record. Under a containment reading these would add occurrences: session/title-llm-request embeds the R1 prompt in a longer request string (all runs); in repetition 1 the diff of the successful edit result holds the old and new snippets inside whole-function text; in repetition 3 two read-call records hold a path that equals the full output of a glob result. Assistant records whose only message content is an empty reasoning block beside a tool call (3, 2, 2 records) count as message events, as in v8. The strictest reading of all four points lowers the row by about 0.15 points; none was treated as a defect.

Density: the first record that states an event keeps its role. The agent/inbox/spliced record is the useful prompt record; user/message, the tool/call records and the cache record are snapshot. A successful edit result that restates its call stays useful because it is the first statement of its result. The assistant/message records include their stream chunk data in useful bytes, as in v8.

Privacy testing is bounded: every 64-hex digest in the three packets (runtime source included) and the bundle was classified with the shared checker (609 public bytes, 6 replay outputs, 38 allowlisted, 0 unbound) and with the reviewer's own script against 541 private and capture-time files (whole file, lines, JSON members) and against public bytes with the real home name put back at depth 1 to 3 (every subset of the three alias forms). No private-derived digest was found among the digests that are not hashes of public bytes, except replay outputs and workload-fixture file digests; the real balance values (31 serialized forms), the digests of the home name, home path and account e-mail, and the digests of the private compressed session file and its decompressed form do not occur; the home name, home path and e-mail do not occur in plain, hex, base64, UTF-16, reversed or upper-case form. Not matched to bytes: four capture-time source digests in parent-capture-manifest.json source_files (dsh_format_evidence.py, dsh_live.py, format_timestamp_population.py, live_observer.py and match no file of the snapshot or of the current working tree). They are allowlisted as repository source; the reviewer accepts the reason but could not read the preimages. A route through a construction the reviewer did not test cannot be excluded.

Residual content judged acceptable: aliased paths that keep the Repository/session-bench layout; ls output with local wall-clock times that reveal a UTC-7 offset; session, message and call identifiers and timestamps; sizes of the zeroed private files; the digest of the system libzstd; capture-source.py naming the credential file location and the balance endpoint without values; a redacted 37-entry skill catalog that keeps entry count and lengths. Packet manifests still say public_safe false; the one-sentence wrapper of the harness title request (about 66 characters) in session/title-llm-request.

attribution.reconciliation is native-attested from the projection cache, which lives outside the session directory and outside the scored root locator, is not listed in required_companions, and is the harness's own fold over all model steps (14, 12 and 12), not over the two displayed responses.

work.changed_files hashes are recomputed from the native inspect result and the native edit call. The pre-image is in the native record because the workload helper prints it, and the decoder does not test for another writer between inspect and edit; none was found in these runs.
Metric locators are whole-file locators. Harness build 0.2.0-rc.2 comes from capture receipts, not from the native session.
